title: Vegan lemon tart
summary: A crisp almond shortbread shell filled with a sharp, smooth coconut lemon cream set with agar; vegan as written.

ingredients.note: cold, cubed; or 3 tbsp solid coconut oil
keeps the cream from turning gritty in the fridge

steps: Make the flax egg and let it rest 10 minutes until gel-like.

Pulse the almond flour, powdered erythritol and salt in a food processor. Add the cold vegan butter and the flax egg and pulse until the dough clumps when pinched. Press it evenly into a 23 cm (9 in) tart tin with a removable base, prick the base and chill 20 minutes.
Heat the oven to 175 °C (350 °F). Bake the shell 14–18 minutes until evenly golden and firm at the edges, covering the rim with foil if it darkens first. Cool completely in the tin.
In a saucepan, whisk the agar into the cold coconut milk until no specks remain, then whisk in the coconut cream, powdered erythritol, allulose, salt, turmeric and zest.
Bring to a full boil over medium heat, whisking, and boil 2 minutes so the agar dissolves completely; the mixture will look thin.
Take the pan off the heat, wait 1 minute, then whisk in the lemon juice. Adding it after the boil keeps the acid from weakening the agar.
Strain at once through a fine sieve into the cooled shell and smooth the top. Work promptly: agar begins to set around 40 °C (104 °F).
Cool 30 minutes at room temperature, then refrigerate at least 3 hours, until the cream is set and cuts cleanly. Slice with a knife dipped in hot water.
tips: Agar sets firmer and cleaner than an egg curd, so the slice is more like a soft panna cotta than a wobbly custard; for a softer cream use 1.5 tsp agar.
If the cream does not set, the agar did not boil long enough: return it to the pan, boil 2 minutes more, add a squeeze of lemon off the heat and pour again.
Taste the mixture before pouring: coconut mutes lemon more than butter and eggs do, so add more zest rather than more juice if you want it sharper.

origin.history: Lemon creams baked in pastry were made in French and English kitchens long before anyone recorded who first made them, and the tarte au citron became a fixture of French pâtisseries without a single credited inventor. The classic cream is set by eggs and enriched with butter. Egg-free versions that set coconut or plant milk with agar, a seaweed gel long used in East Asian sweets, spread with vegan baking in the 2000s and 2010s.
